title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 23-25 of cote 150). Grothendieck is setting up an axiomatic, purely topological theory of stratified spaces. A space X with a closed stratum Y carries a germ of conical structure T. This means a conical neighbourhood T of Y with boundary Ṫ, a retraction Ṫ→Y, and 'homotheties' λ_T for λ∈[0,1] that contract T onto Y. The theory is 'déploiement': unfolding (X,Y,T) into a space X̃ with boundary Ẋ together with a map Ẋ→Y. On this page he defines when a second structure is compatible with T. That second structure is a 'bordante' (bounding) subspace X_0⊂X with a germ of cylindrical structure (collar) E≅X_0×I.

The definition (finishing p.23) has three parts.
(a) E meets T, Ṫ and Y cylindrically: T∩E≅T_0×I, Ṫ∩E≅Ṫ_0×I and Y∩E≅Y_0×I, where T_0=T∩X_0, Ṫ_0=Ṫ∩X_0, Y_0=Y∩X_0.
(b) Symmetrically, E∩T, Ė∩T and X_0∩T=T_0 are conical subspaces of T, hence stable under the T-homotheties. Via (a) they are T_0×I, T_0×{1} and T_0×{0}.
(c) The homotheties λ_E and λ_T commute on T∩E. Consequently λ_T induces one and the same operation λ_{T_0} on T_0×{0} and on T_0×{1}, and λ_T on T∩E≅T_0×I is λ_{T_0}×id_I.

He then condenses (a)-(c) into an equivalent condition. There must be a homeomorphism T∩E≅T_0×I, compatible with E≅X_0×I and inducing Ṫ∩E≅Ṫ_0×I and Y∩E≅Y_0×I. Under it, the conical structure of T over Y restricts on T_E over Y_E to the product by I of a conical structure of T_0 over Y_0⊂T_0.

In words: near the boundary piece X_0, the cone bundle over Y is a product of a cone bundle over Y_0 with the collar coordinate. This is the topological analogue of Thom-Mather commuting tubular neighbourhoods and control data, here between a collar and a conical neighbourhood. It is the input for the next page, p.25. There he proves a proposition: collars compatible with T correspond to compatible collars upstairs on the unfolded space X̃ and downstairs on Y, compatible with the projection Ẋ→Y. That is a step in showing that the unfolding is compatible with restriction to boundary pieces, in the spirit of an induction on strata.
errors: The first lines write 'Y∩E ≃ Y_0∩E'. Per the rest of the page and p.23 this should be Y∩E ≃ Y_0×I.
On p.23 he writes Y_0 = Ẋ_0∩Y, while here Y_0 = Y∩X_0. The latter is the consistent definition.

The parameter range 'λ∈[0,1]' in (c) presumably should be ]0,1] for the invertible part. For λ=0 the T-homothety collapses onto Y, and the product statement there is the retraction T_0→Y_0 times id_I. This is harmless.

The equivalence of (a)-(c) with the condensed product condition is asserted, not proved. It is essentially tautological once the identifications are fixed, though one must choose the homeomorphism compatibly with both structures.

ideas.what: Compatibility of a collar (cylindrical germ) of a bounding subspace with a conical-neighbourhood germ of a stratum: commuting homotheties, with the conical structure locally a product with the collar coordinate.
ideas.modern_name: Commuting/controlled tubular neighbourhoods and collars; control data (Thom-Mather); compatible collars on manifolds with corners
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970/2012 notes); for topological collars Brown/Connelly; for stratified collars Siebenmann (1972), Quinn (1988)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6

ideas.what: Déploiement: unfolding a conically stratified space (X,Y,T) into (X̃, Ẋ, collar, Ẋ→Y), with compatibility of further structures (collars, closed subspaces) transported to the unfolded data.
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / resolution of conically stratified spaces into manifolds with corners (blow-up along strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces, 2017); earlier Verona, Thom-Mather resolution/'déploiement' ideas; Melrose for corners
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to tame stratified structures and their dévissage; details not published

missed.claim: The page works out, purely topologically and with homotheties rather than distance functions, the compatibility needed to make 'unfolding' (déploiement) functorial with respect to collared boundary pieces. This is the same technical point addressed decades later in Ayala-Francis-Tanaka's unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces. The definition itself is routine, but the overall programme anticipates that framework.
missed.quote: la structure cônique de T sur Y induit sur T_E sur Y_E la structure cônique produit par I, d'une structure cônique de T_0 sur Y_0⊂T_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest. It documents that Grothendieck developed an axiomatic conical/cylindrical-germ formalism for unfolding stratified spaces in 1981-82, predating the AFT approach. The page itself contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine definitional step: a collar is compatible with a conical neighbourhood when the commuting homotheties make the cone structure a product with I. It is analogous to well-known Thom-Mather control conditions. Its interest is only as part of the unpublished déploiement programme.
transcription_corrections: 'Y∩E} ≃ Y_0∩E' in the image is a slip for Y∩E ≃ Y_0×I. The transcription reproduces the manuscript, but the intended meaning should be noted.
'Dans les conditions a) b) c) ignorées [?] : celles-ci :' is likely 'Donc les conditions a) b) c) équivalent à celles-ci :'.
's'identifie, une = opération de T_0→T_0' likely reads 's'identifie, une même opération de T_0 → T_0'.
The final line reads 'T_0 sur Y_0⊂T_0, [par I struck]', with 'par I' inserted earlier after 'cônique produit'. This is consistent with the transcription.
